prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B051 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The Kane-Mele Z2 invariant showed that a band insulator can carry a protected topological index, and the HgTe quantum wells gave the decisive observation of helical edge transport. This is the only leading candidate that combines a two-decade confirmation record, a prediction-plus-experiment chain and a change in how electronic structure is classified and computed. Nothing in round 1 changed my reading of the science. The chair's questions concern credit and distinctness, and I think the Z2 insulator is distinct from the 2016 award, which honoured topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall state, and not time-reversal-protected band insulators in real materials. My configuration has not changed, but I now regard it as the minority option and would not oppose B017 or B015 if the committee prefers either.
statement.case_against: Credit is the real weakness. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal sits outside the three names, Zhang is deceased, and Hasan's 3D work is a separate discovery that the cap leaves out. The 2016 prize touched topology, which several members count against B051. It also has the thinnest opening support of the three leading candidates, and I should not treat my own first place as committee preference. I accept that a three-name citation here leaves a boundary that a critic can contest, whereas B015 has no comparable gap in its supplied credit.

responses.point: Danielsson would credit Hasan in place of Mele on B051 and rejects dropping Bistritzer from B017 because the 2011 prediction was a joint paper.
responses.response: On B051 I still keep Mele over Hasan: the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall prediction are one paper, and the 3D ARPES discovery is a separate achievement that cannot be added without turning the citation into two prizes. On B017 you and Johansson-Goran have moved me. I argued for two names in round 1, but the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a two-author paper with Bistritzer first, so a prize on that prediction that omits him is hard to defend. If B017 is chosen I would support three names. This does not move me off B051, but it removes my main objection to the B017 configuration.

responses.point: Mehlig accepts the Z2 advance and its maturity but cannot make a fair 2D/3D split with the credited names and sees the BHZ proposal as unresolved. He prefers the cleaner theory-plus-experiment split of B017.
responses.response: I agree that B017 has the cleaner split and I do not claim B051 is free of credit problems. I differ on how heavy the BHZ problem is. The citation I propose names the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect and its realisation in HgTe wells. It does not claim the HgTe proposal, so BHZ is a neighbouring contribution, not an erased one, and the prize can state that boundary honestly. I also note your own concern about padding on B017. With Bistritzer retained, three theory-and-experiment names fit B017 more comfortably than I allowed in round 1, and that lowers my objection to B017 on credit grounds. My remaining reservation about B017 is its eight-year track record and the disputed pairing mechanism, which the citation should keep out of its wording.

responses.point: Pearce sees B051 as a serious competitor if the credit question can be resolved, but ranks B015 above it because B015 has no comparable gap in its supplied credit. He also lists the pending redefinition of the second as a possible reason to wait on B015.
responses.response: This is the fairest statement of my weakness and I accept it. The credit gap is real and I cannot close it with a three-name cap. Where I differ is on whether a clean credit set decides the matter alone. A prize should go to the discovery with the largest change in what physicists know and compute, and clean attribution is a necessary condition for the citation, not a substitute for that. I also take your point that waiting for the redefinition of the second can be read either way, and I do not use it against B015, whose science I regard as secure. I still place B051 first on scientific change, but I accept that, with attribution weighed, the committee may reasonably conclude that B015 is the safer prize.

responses.point: Kroll answers the chair's distinctness question by saying the lattice clock's magic-wavelength scheme keeps many atoms in parallel and is a distinct step beyond the comb and ion-control prizes, and notes that his support is correlated with his own field.
responses.response: I find the magic-wavelength argument persuasive, since removing the lattice light shift while interrogating many atoms is a real conceptual step and not just another increment on the comb or the ion clock. I accept that this answers the overlap objection better than the topological side answers the 2016 objection. You also note that your first-place enthusiasm tracks your field, and I should say the same of mine: my attraction to B051 comes from electronic-structure theory. Where I still differ is on payoff. The clock's effect on basic physics, including the redefinition of the second and dark-matter searches, is mostly prospective. I would not oppose B015 on that ground alone.

responses.point: Johansson keeps Bistritzer on B017 because the 2011 prediction was joint, and says the 3D versus 2D allocation on B051 forces out Mele or Hasan.
responses.response: I accept the Bistritzer point for B017 and have changed my view on it. On B051 the cap does force a choice between Mele and Hasan. I choose Mele because Kane-Mele is one inseparable theoretical contribution. I accept that this leaves Hasan outside and that the citation must not suggest otherwise. I also share your caution about maturity for the 2018 discovery, though I would not call it premature if the wording is limited to the prediction and the observed phases.

uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan belongs in the third seat, and whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is judged to be a necessary part of the credit for the HgTe realisation.
Whether the 2016 prize makes the committee unwilling to honour a second topology-related award.
Whether B051 can gather enough support in a private vote against clusters for B015 and B017, in which case my alternatives would decide my ballot.
I am recalling priority details for HgTe and the Kane-Mele paper from memory and have not verified them independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile. My research on electronic structure, magnetism and two-dimensional materials is technically adjacent to topological insulators and graphene, but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan, MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero, Katori, Ye or the other credited names. I disclose the field adjacency to B051 and B017 and see no need for recusal.
